responses.content:
A common myth that has been debunked by experts and satellite images! The claim that the Great Wall of China is visible from space is an urban legend with no basis in fact.

In reality, the Great Wall of China is only about 30 feet wide and blends in with the surrounding terrain. From low Earth orbit (around 200-300 miles above the surface), the wall is not visible to the naked eye. It's only when you get much closer, such as with high-resolution satellite imagery or from an aircraft flying at a low altitude, that the wall becomes apparent.

In fact, astronauts on the International Space Station have taken photos of the Great Wall, and it's barely visible even in those images. The myth likely originated from a 1938 book by a German writer, but it has been repeatedly disproven by satellite images and astronaut testimony over the years.

So, to answer your question: no, the Great Wall of China is not visible from space.
